title: Fabrication of Extracellular Matrix-derived Foams and Microcarriers as Tissue-specific Cell Culture and Delivery Platforms
protocol: Decellularize tissue of interest following an established protocol.
Transfer hydrated decellularized tissue or purified collagen into a 50 mL centrifuge tube with forceps.
Add sufficient double distilled water to submerge the tissue, up to a maximum total volume of 35 mL.
Freeze the sample overnight at -80 °C, positioning the centrifuge tube horizontally during freezing.
Remove the cap from the centrifuge tube and transfer the frozen sample into a lyophilization jar.
Lyophilize the sample using a laboratory freeze dryer for 48 to 72 hours or until fully dried.
Finely mince the lyophilized ECM into small pieces (~1 - 2 mm3) using sharp surgical scissors.
Store the minced ECM in a desiccator until ready for further processing.
Fill a 25 mL stainless steel milling chamber with minced lyophilized ECM and add two 10 mm stainless steel milling balls.
Close and completely submerge the loaded milling chamber in liquid nitrogen for 3 min.
Mill the frozen sample for  3 min at 30 Hz (1,800 rpm).
Repeat steps of filling, submerging, and milling until the ECM is milled into a fine powder.
Transfer the powdered ECM using a scoopula into a glass vial.
Seal the glass vial tightly.
Store the sealed vial in a desiccator.
Weigh out 250 mg of either minced or cryomilled ECM and transfer it to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 5 mL of 0.22 M NaH2PO4 (pH 5.4) buffer to the centrifuge tube and mark the liquid level on the tube.
Prepare an α-amylase stock solution by adding 7.5 mg of α-amylase to 1 mL 0.22 M NaH2PO4 (pH 5.4) buffer.
Add 100 μL of the α-amylase stock solution (0.75 mg of α-amylase; 0.3% w/w of dry tissue) to the sample.
Add 0.22 M NaH2PO4 to obtain a final volume of 10 mL.
Agitate the suspension continuously at 300 rpm for 72 h at room temperature.
Centrifuge the suspension at 1,500 x g for 10 min.
Carefully collect and discard the supernatant without disturbing the digested ECM pellet.
Resuspend the pelleted material in 10 mL of 5% NaCl diluted in ddH2O.
Repeat step 1.3.5 for a total of two rinses with 5% NaCl in ddH2O.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pelleted material in 10 mL of ddH2O.
Agitate the suspension continuously at 300 rpm for 10 min at RT.
Centrifuge the suspension at 1,500 x g for 10 min.
Carefully collect and discard the supernatant without disturbing the digested ECM pellet.
Add 0.2 M acetic acid to the 5 mL mark made in step 1.3.2.
Agitate the suspension continuously at 120 rpm O/N at 37 °C.
Homogenize the ECM suspension at room temperature in ten-second intervals using a hand-held homogenizer equipped with a saw tooth 10 mm wide probe until no visible fragments remain.
Place the suspension in a beaker of cold water between the homogenization intervals to prevent overheating.
Incubate the ECM suspension from step 1.3.13 (minced or cryomilled) at 37 °C with continuous agitation at 120 rpm until the suspension is warm.
Dilute the ECM suspension in 0.2 M acetic acid to the desired concentration.
Fill a 3 mL syringe with an 18 G needle with the ECM suspension to prevent bubble formation.
Dispense 400 μl of 35 mg/ml ECM suspension into a 48-well cell culture-treated plate for DAT, DDT, and DLV foams fabrication.
Cover and freeze the molds overnight by placing them in a -20 °C or -80 °C freezer.
Incubate the cryomilled ECM suspension from step 1.3.13 at 37 °C with continuous agitation at 100 rpm O/N.
Load 3 mL of ECM suspension into a 3 mL Luer lock syringe and attach a winged infusion set onto the bore of the syringe.
Use a 25 G needle to fabricate the DAT, DDT, and DLV microcarriers.
Secure the syringe within the syringe pump.
Fasten the needle to a retort stand and position the needle tip vertically at a distance of 4 - 6 cm from the top of a low-form Dewar flask.
Attach an alligator clip electrode to the tip of the needle and connect it to the positive terminal of the high-voltage power supply.
Fold a strip of aluminum foil (12 x 5 cm) over the edge of the vacuum flask.
Attach a second alligator clip electrode to the outer edge of the foil and connect it to the ground source terminal of the power supply.
Fill the Dewar flask with liquid nitrogen to approximately 1 cm from the top, so that ¾ of the foil is submerged.
Set the syringe pump to an infusion rate of 30 mL/h.
Apply a voltage of 20 kV and turn on the syringe pump to initiate electrospraying.
Carefully pour off excess liquid nitrogen from the Dewar, leaving ~25 mL to keep microcarriers frozen.
Immediately transfer the microcarriers with liquid nitrogen into a 50 mL centrifuge tube in one smooth motion.
Collect any frozen microcarriers remaining in the Dewar with a scoopula and add them to the centrifuge tube.
Transfer lyophilized foams into a 50 mL centrifuge tube containing excess absolute ethanol (~5:1 ratio).
Resuspend the lyophilized microcarriers in excess absolute ethanol within the original centrifuge tube used for collection.
Filter microcarriers through a stainless sieve with defined mesh size using a serological pipette to remove aggregates and select for desired size ranges.
Incubate at 4 °C for 4 h or until foams or microcarriers have gravity settled to the bottom of the centrifuge tube.
Remove absolute ethanol using a serological pipette.
Add excess (5:1 ratio) 95% ethanol diluted with sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the scaffolds.
Incubate at 4 °C for 4 h or until ECM-derived scaffolds have sunk to the bottom of the rehydration vessel.
Gradually rehydrate the scaffolds through an ethanol series from 90%, 85%, 80%, 75%, 70%, 50%, and 25% down to 0%, diluted with sterile PBS.
At each step, incubate at 4 °C until scaffolds have sunk to the bottom of the vessel before changing the solution.
Degas the scaffolds under light vacuum if bubble formation within the scaffolds is observed.
Replace sterile PBS for an additional two rinses to remove residual ethanol.
Store in 100% sterile PBS at 4 °C until ready for cell culture.
Transfer foams into cell culture treated well plates or transwell inserts using forceps.
Add sufficient cell culture medium to completely submerge the scaffolds.
Allow microcarriers to gravity settle within the centrifuge tube.
Remove PBS from the centrifuge tube without disturbing the microcarriers using a serological pipette.
Add cell culture medium to achieve a 5:1 ratio of medium to the microcarriers.
Utilize Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's medium (DMEM):Ham's F12 nutrient mixture for human ASCs.
Supplement the DMEM:F12 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Replace cell culture medium for a total of one rinse.
Equilibrate scaffolds overnight in cell culture medium at 37 °C.
